Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: After I was nomianted for a spot I rememeber having to filling out some information online, not much else.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There was an online meeting with a presentation going over all the information. But when my home university sent my over my nomantion later, this had already happened. And I remember being quite nervous about how everything was going to be filled in. It was only when I wrote to the host institution that they informed me that there had been an online meeting. It had luckly been recorded and was shared with me. So it all worked out. Just a bit odd that I had to ask for it.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Reasonably successful. I did as recommended by the host university and applied for 35 ECTS credits, even though I only needed 30. This was done so that if one subject was rejected, you didn't have to wait any longer. And that's exactly what happened. I was rejected from one subject and only had 30 ECTS credits left. It was a bit stressful because I was afraid of doing something wrong. But I think the host university was really good at informing me about everything I needed.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: To apply for 35 ECTS even though only 30 is needed, beacuse then you won't need to reapply if one course is rejected. Checking your email often and keeping track of things. There are many deadlines to meet. Contact the university if you have any questions, they are really good at guiding you through it all.
